thesis: Anthropic listed on Nasdaq on Nov 19 at an $83 IPO price, opened at $111.50 and has since swung widely (today +10.8% to ~$91.74 after Wednesday's close of $82.79); the 60-day move is computed over only ~5 real trading bars, so it reflects post-IPO price discovery rather than an established trend, and the trend filter could not be applied. This run found several lawsuits filed just before pricing (a Nov 12 nonprofit suit in San Francisco Superior Court naming multiple AI labs, a Flinn AI patent suit, a music-publisher piracy suit, a Sept antitrust class action) but no scheduled ruling or hearing within ~90 days, and staged lock-up releases are pending with no schedule found. The price action is largely sentiment-driven, which suggests waiting for a real trading history before any entry.
invalidation: A sustained trading history (enough real bars to apply the trend filter) holding above the IPO-week range, plus a first public-company earnings report confirming growth

thesis: Held position. Linde is up ~11% over 60 days and trades ~2.8% below its 52-week high, comfortably above its 200-day MA. The most recent company disclosure, Q3 2026 results, showed net income down 12% and diluted EPS down 11% to $3.66, while the board declared a $1.60 quarterly dividend (record Dec 3); this run found no fresh company-specific catalyst explaining the run-up, so the price strength and the weaker reported earnings leave the read mixed. No scheduled litigation or governance event surfaced. Trend still supports holding, at limited conviction.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or a guidance cut at the next quarterly report

thesis: Southern Co. is up ~15% over 60 days and trades ~4.6% below its 52-week high, above its 200-day MA. Company-disclosed Q3 results showed data-center electricity sales up ~52% year over year, supporting the load-growth story; however this is offset by a newly Democratic-majority Georgia PSC and a governor-elect who campaigned on a temporary data-center moratorium, which suggests heightened regulatory risk on bills and large-load contracts. No scheduled ruling/hearing within ~90 days or governance event surfaced. Net read is mixed, so the trend is intact but conviction is limited.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or Georgia PSC action restricting data-center contracts / rate recovery

thesis: McDonald's is up ~21% over 60 days off its Oct 5 52-week low ($229.20) and now sits just above its 200-day MA. The Nov 4 Q3 report beat on adjusted EPS ($3.57 vs $3.38) and global comps rose 1.5%, but revenue missed and U.S. comps fell 0.2% on weak traffic, the first U.S. decline in five quarters; management declined to promise better Q4 U.S. sales and the broader value program isn't national until early 2027. The evidence is mixed, so the recovery rally suggests a rebound from oversold levels rather than a clear fundamental re-rating. No scheduled litigation or governance event surfaced.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or another quarter of negative U.S. comparable sales

thesis: Home Depot is up ~25% over 60 days and trades ~8.9% below its 52-week high, well above its 200-day MA. Its Nov 17 fiscal Q3 2026 release (8-K) showed sales +4.9% to $43.4B, comparable sales +2.2% (accelerating from 1.7% in Q2) and adjusted EPS $3.86 vs $3.74, with full-year comp guidance lifted to ~1.4% from flat-to-2%. Counter-evidence: comparable transactions fell 0.5% and adjusted operating margin slipped to 13.0% from 13.3%, and much of the 60-day move preceded the report (shares were roughly flat on the day), so the rally also likely reflects housing/rate sentiment. A real company-specific catalyst exists, but multiple drivers are contributing without one clearly dominant. No scheduled litigation or governance event surfaced.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or a comp-sales guidance cut at the next (fiscal Q4) report

thesis: Held position. Costco is up ~18% over 60 days and trades ~2.2% below its 52-week high, well above its 200-day MA. The company's Nov 4 release reported October net sales of $24.50B (+12.6%), total comps +11.1% (+7.3% ex gas/FX) and digital sales +22.5%, a confirmed company-specific driver. The strongest counter-case is valuation (~46x forward P/E vs ~30x industry) with downward earnings revisions noted by Zacks; that risk is named but not clearly resolved by this run's evidence. No scheduled litigation or governance event surfaced. Read still supports holding.
invalidation: Comparable sales ex gas/FX decelerating below ~4%, or a close back below the 200-day MA

thesis: P&G trades within ~0.9% of its 52-week high after a ~16% 60-day move, well above its 200-day MA. Available analysis (Trefis) attributes the rally mainly to P/E expansion (to ~24.7x from ~20.2x a year ago) rather than a newly disclosed fundamental catalyst, which suggests a rotation into defensives rather than a company-specific re-rating. The next earnings report is Jan 21, 2027. No scheduled ruling/hearing within ~90 days or governance event surfaced in this run. Trend is intact but the driver is not company-specific.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or an organic-sales miss / guidance cut at the Jan 21 report

thesis: Held position. Lilly is up ~17.5% over 60 days, ~5.4% below its Nov 16 52-week high and far above its 200-day MA. Confirmed company-specific drivers include regulatory approvals of oral GLP-1 Foundayo (orforglipron) in the U.S. and China and new Zepbound/Foundayo/retatrutide data presented at ObesityWeek (Nov 14-17). Counter-considerations (competition from Novo's oral pill, low-price access strategy weighing on per-unit economics, rich valuation) are present but not resolved one way or the other by this run's research. No scheduled litigation or governance event surfaced. Read still supports holding.
invalidation: A material safety signal or prescription-uptake miss for Foundayo/Zepbound, or a close back below the 200-day MA

thesis: Held position. Visa is up ~15% over 60 days and trades ~2.8% below its 52-week high, well above its 200-day MA. This run's search did not surface a fresh company-specific catalyst behind the move, so the strength appears tied to broader payments/financials sentiment. The DOJ debit-monopolization suit (motion to dismiss denied) remains open, but no trial date has been set and DOJ filings point to trial in late 2027 or later, so it doesn't meet the active_litigation threshold. Trend supports holding at limited conviction.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or an adverse development/settlement in the DOJ debit case that impairs debit economics

thesis: SK hynix ADRs are down ~39% over 60 days and trade ~40% below the 52-week high (the trend filter could not be applied with only 98 real daily bars). The selloff has run alongside a broad memory-stock rout even as reported fundamentals stayed strong (Q3 revenue ~KRW 104.6T, ~80% operating margin, DRAM ASPs up high-20s% q/q, capacity largely contracted through 2028), so the decline reads as sentiment- and positioning-driven rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration. This run did not surface the export-license or class-action items with a scheduled step. Evidence is mixed: price trend argues against entry while fundamentals argue the opposite.
invalidation: A sustained reversal with enough real bars to pass the trend filter, or confirmation of continued memory-price strength in the next quarterly report

thesis: Held position. Apple trades within ~0.6% of its 52-week (and all-time) intraday high of $360.83 set Nov 13, far above its 200-day MA. The company-disclosed fiscal Q4 showed record September-quarter revenue of $114.5B (+12%). Counter-evidence: management guided to lower holiday-quarter margins on what CEO John Ternus called 'unprecedented' memory pricing, and the stock trades above most analyst targets; the stock has nonetheless made new highs since that guidance, which suggests the margin concern is being absorbed, though it isn't fully resolved. No scheduled litigation or governance event surfaced. Read still supports holding.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or a holiday-quarter result showing gross margin compression beyond guidance

thesis: SpaceX is down ~12% over 60 days and sits ~41% below its June high; the trend filter could not be applied (116 real daily bars). This run found a Nov 5 ~9% drop tied to post-election concerns about heightened scrutiny of Musk-linked businesses and a weakened Tesla-merger narrative, weakness alongside the AI-stock selloff, and a disclosed insider lockup expiry on Dec 8 that could add tradable supply. No lawsuit with a scheduled step surfaced. With a pending supply overhang and a weak tape, the setup suggests avoiding a new entry for now.
invalidation: Lockup expiry passing without pressure and a sustained recovery above ~$150, or a confirmed company-specific positive catalyst (e.g. disclosed government contract)

thesis: DoubleVerify (market-scan candidate) trades at ~$13.615 against Nielsen's definitive all-cash offer of $13.60 per share (announced Aug 6, 2026; company 8-K), i.e. at or slightly above the deal price, and today's ~8x volume spike and razor-thin range suggest merger-arbitrage activity near closing. Upside is capped by the fixed cash consideration while downside remains if the deal breaks; closing is still subject to shareholder approval and remaining regulatory clearances, and merger disclosure suits/demand letters were reported (no scheduled hearing found). The asymmetry suggests avoiding a new entry.
invalidation: A competing bid or raised offer above $13.60, or deal termination resetting the stock on standalone fundamentals
